items.title: MECH-489 (SD-099) defensive-orienting decision retest after SD-ORIENTING-DECISION-SCALE fix
items.note: Re-queue of V3-EXQ-910 (script copied, not edited in place -- v3_exq_910_mech489_defensive_orienting_validation.py is preserved unchanged as the exact historical record of that run) after implementing SD-ORIENTING-DECISION-SCALE via /implement-substrate this session (docs/architecture/sd_orienting_decision_scale.md, ree_core/agent.py select_action() Component 4/5). failure_autopsy_V3-EXQ-910_2026-08-10.md found MECH-489's Component 4/5 (approach/withdraw/resume decision) confounded by a norm-vs-value scale mismatch (structurally non-negative z_harm_s L2 norm compared directly against a near-zero-unless-close benefit RBF value), which biased every override toward withdraw regardless of actual event valence (206/206 logged overrides in V3-EXQ-910). Fix: both channels now z-scored against their own running mean/mean-absolute-deviation (EMA, frozen while orienting is active) before comparison. SCOPE: this re-queue tests ONLY the valence-gating sub-component (Components 4/5) -- MECH-489's trigger-alignment sub-claim (Components 1-3, pass criteria (a)/(b), unchanged by this fix) already stands as fairly falsified per its own pre-registered signature in the autopsy and is NOT being re-litigated; those criteria are still computed (script reuses the identical 906b substrate/curriculum unmodified) and reported for context, but the run's decisive test is a NEW criterion (c) added for this re-queue: C_decision_alignment_non_degenerate, which requires the resolved decision NOT be unconditionally one class (V3-EXQ-910's bug signature was 0 approach / 0 resume / 206 withdraw). New readiness precondition pooled_overrides_count_sufficient (>=5 pooled Component-4/5 overrides across ON-arm seeds) gates criterion (c)'s meaningfulness, mirroring the existing per-event-field readiness preconditions. GOV-REUSE-1: the decisive readout (decision_alignment as a function of the FIXED comparison logic) does not exist in any prior manifest -- the fix did not exist before this session; not recoverable by reanalysis, a run is required. Re-derive brake (2.5b): MECH-489 autopsy count against substrate_ceiling = 0 (the one prior autopsy read a code-bug confound, not a ceiling) -- brake does not fire. Substrate-path overlap gate (2.5c): no open corrupting substrate_queue.json entry other than this one (now implemented_pending_validation) touches ree_core/agent.py or this driver's other imports. Smoke: validate_experiments.py --strict OK (0 warnings after adding an explicit "direction": "lower" to the new precondition). --dry-run confirms wiring (no crash, progress instrumentation correct, z_goal_stream active_frac=0.998 no writer defect, new precondition correctly reports measured=0/threshold=5/met=False at toy dry-run scale) and correctly self-routes substrate_not_ready_requeue at toy scale (0 injected events in 2x30-step segments, same expected pattern as V3-EXQ-910's own dry-run and 906b's). Queued via /implement-substrate's mandatory Step 8 -> /queue-experiment handoff, IGW-20260810-210, chip chip-igw-20260810-210.
